_comment: One object per eval run, newest last. Each references an eval in registry.json by `eval`. `metrics` keys must match that eval's metric keys. `date` is the run date (YYYY-MM-DD); `run_id` is unique within an eval. The /evals hub plots each metric across the runs of its eval, so appending a run here is all it takes to extend the trend graphs. Keep `counts` for the raw numbers behind rate metrics. Optional `scorecard` links this run's own report page (e.g. /evals/scorecard?run=<run_id>, served from eval/golden_scorecard_<run_id>.html); the hub lists one link per run, falling back to the eval's scorecard path + ?run= when absent.

runs.label: Golden set v1
runs.notes: First full golden run: 50 personas, top-10 ranked each. Scored by the LLM-judge pre-labels in golden_matches_scored.csv. See the full scorecard for per-row verdicts.

runs.label: Golden set v1
runs.notes: Second full golden run (same 50 personas, top-10 ranked each), scored by the LLM-judge pre-labels. Re-run of the live suggest pipeline; verdicts are model pre-labels, not ground truth. See the full scorecard for per-row verdicts. METHODOLOGY NOTE: this and the 2026-09-02 run are UN-CURATED — the harness padded each profile to 10 with blank-blurb rows the app actually drops (finder curation, commit 6e49034). Not directly comparable to 2026-09-04+, which curate to reranker-vouched rows (MARQUEE M10).

runs.label: Curated (M10)
runs.notes: First PRODUCTION-ACCURATE run: the harness now curates to reranker-vouched rows exactly as the finder does (MARQUEE M10), so results = what students actually see. 158 blank-blurb padding rows the app drops are gone (500 -> 342 shown), which is why good-match rate rises sharply and blank/wrong fall to ~0 vs the un-curated 09-02/09-03 runs — a measurement-method correction, not a same-basis quality jump. Verdicts are LLM-judge pre-labels, not ground truth.
